label: Battery and charging
pick_label: The laptop is not charging, or the battery drains fast

c_start.text: What is the problem? If anything smells burnt, feels very hot or looks swollen, unplug the laptop and stop using it.
c_start.why: Charging problems and fast draining have different checks.

c_cable.title: Check the charger, cable and outlet
c_cable.do: Check the charger is firmly plugged into the laptop and the wall. Try a different wall outlet that works for something else. Look at the charger and cable for fraying or bent pins; if you see damage, stop using it.
c_cable.why: A loose plug, a dead outlet or a damaged cable is the most common reason a laptop does not charge.
c_cable.expect: The charging light turns on or the battery icon shows a charging symbol.

c_done_cable.cause: A loose connection or a faulty outlet.
c_done_cable.learn: The charger changes wall power into low-voltage power for the laptop. If any part of that chain is loose or damaged, charging stops.

c_port.caution: Make sure the laptop is off and unplugged first. Never use metal, and do not force anything into the port.
c_port.title: Check the charging port for lint
c_port.do: Turn the laptop off and unplug it. Shine a light into the charging port. If you see lint or dust, gently remove it with a wooden toothpick or a short burst of compressed air. Never use metal.
c_port.why: Lint packed into the port can stop the plug from making full contact.
c_port.expect: The plug seats firmly and charging starts.

c_done_port.cause: Lint or dust blocking the charger connection.
c_done_port.learn: The plug has to reach the contacts at the back of the port. A small amount of packed lint can stop it from reaching them.

c_reset.title: Do a power reset
c_reset.do: Turn the laptop off and unplug the charger. Hold the power button for 30 seconds. Plug in only the charger and turn the laptop on.
c_reset.why: Holding the power button drains leftover charge and clears a stuck power state.
c_reset.expect: The laptop may start more slowly and then show the charging symbol.

c_done_reset.cause: A stuck power or charging state.
c_done_reset.learn: Power management chips keep a small state in memory. A power reset clears it so charging can be detected again.

c_driver.caution: Only uninstall the battery item named in this step. Windows installs it again when you restart.
c_driver.title: Reinstall the battery driver
c_driver.do: Right-click Start and open Device Manager. Expand 'Batteries', right-click 'Microsoft ACPI-Compliant Control Method Battery' and choose 'Uninstall device'. Restart the computer; Windows installs it again.
c_driver.why: Windows installs a fresh battery driver at startup, which can fix a battery that is stuck at not charging.
c_driver.expect: The battery icon updates after the restart.

c_done_driver.learn: Windows reads the battery level through a driver. If the driver gets stuck, it can show 'plugged in, not charging'.

c_apps.title: See what is using your battery
c_apps.do: Open Settings > System > Power & battery > Battery usage. Look for apps using a large share of the battery, and close or uninstall the ones you do not need.
c_apps.why: One busy app in the background can drain the battery quickly.
c_apps.expect: You can see which apps use the most power.

c_done_apps.cause: A background app using a lot of power.
c_done_apps.learn: Apps that keep the processor, screen or network busy use more energy. Finding and closing them is the quickest way to extend battery life.

c_saver.title: Turn on Battery saver and lower brightness
c_saver.do: Open Settings > System > Power & battery. Turn on Battery saver, lower the screen brightness, and shorten the screen timeout.
c_saver.why: The screen is usually the biggest user of battery power, and Battery saver limits background activity.
c_saver.expect: The battery lasts longer between charges.

c_done_saver.cause: High screen brightness and background activity.
c_done_saver.learn: Brightness and background tasks have a big effect on battery life. Lowering them often adds an hour or more.

c_health.text: Open Command Prompt and run powercfg /batteryreport, then open the report file it names. Is the 'Full charge capacity' much lower than the 'Design capacity' (for example, under 60%)?
c_health.why: This compares how much charge the battery holds now with how much it held when new.

options.label: No, it is close to the design capacity

c_pro_charge.reason: The safe checks did not restore charging. The charger, the charging port or the battery may be at fault. If you can borrow a matching charger from the maker, trying it helps tell them apart.

c_pro_worn.reason: The battery now holds much less charge than when it was new, which is normal wear. Many laptop batteries are built in, so replacement is best done by a technician or the maker.

c_pro_drain.reason: The battery capacity looks healthy, but it still drains quickly. A technician can look at background software, heat and power settings in more detail.
